presentation.row_diagrams: Fixed real SRAG receivers, selected as the first adult records per observed outcome, are a window into the first registered full temporal-test permutation. Donor values come from all evaluation rows. Original receiver inputs and predictions stay unchanged; recorded predictions are replayed, not calculated by XGBoost in the browser.
presentation.results: The mechanism error chart uses the original global Brier and the repeated full-test mean and sample shuffle SD. The displayed first global repetition is identified separately. Receiver losses are audited in notebooks, not used as the chart estimate. Ranking and repeat trace use the same complete temporal evaluation.
presentation.source_figures: modules/00-dataset/notebooks/srag_pfi_ranking.ipynb sections 9, 11 and 14; exported SVG copies unchanged.
presentation.teaching_source: modules/06-pfi/evidence/pfi_teaching_demo.json, generated by tools/srag_73_teaching_demo.py in pfi_walkthrough.ipynb §3 and independently reproduced in pfi_internals.ipynb §5. tools/srag_72_pfi_presentation.py explicitly projects it into data/pfi-teaching-records.json and checks first global errors against modules/00-dataset/gold/pfi_ranking.json.
presentation.historical_teaching_source: modules/00-dataset/gold/pfi_slide_explainer.json preview is preserved unchanged. Its manual subset order and measured losses document the previous mechanism and its correction; they do not feed the current animation.

included_data: Separate aggregate and teaching-window files. Aggregates contain global errors, ranking summaries, repeat traces, study counts and fixed-model protocol. The teaching window contains unchanged receiver inputs/outcomes, original and first-global-repeat probabilities/classes/squared errors, received input values and global permutation protocol. Received values are real, while permuted records are artificial combinations. No source identifiers, dates, location fields, donor identifiers/positions/outcomes, contingency tables, subgroup tables or snapshots; identifier omission is not a claim of anonymization.
